title: CNC drilling machine hydraulic requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Port-level repaired two-valve, pressure-compensated open-circuit topology. Tank.S feeds Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P, ClampDCV.P, and DrillDCV.P; ReliefValve.T, both DCV tank ports, and both sequence-valve drains return directly to Tank.R. ClampDCV controls the clamp through a dual pilot-operated check mounted at the clamp cylinder ports; ClampDCV float-center neutral vents the load-lock valve-side lines so the checks can reseat during the clamp-hold/drilling condition. ForwardSequenceValve gates the drill cap supply and is externally piloted from the held clamp cap-side pressure downstream of the load lock, so the phase transition from clamp extension/completion to drilling changes the forward sequence valve from closed to open. DrillFeedFlowControl remains the single non-compensated one-way flow control in the drill rod-side exhaust meter-out path. ReverseSequenceValve gates clamp release and is externally piloted from the DrillDCV.B retract-supply side of the drill rod branch, downstream of the directional valve and on the low-pressure/tank side during drill feed extension, avoiding false release from rod-side meter-out backpressure; it is selected open only after drill retraction is completed and retract-line pressure rises to the sequence setting.

motion_control_decisions.justification: The stated clamp speed is a numeric performance target only; the user clarified the clamp axis is horizontal and purely resistive, so no special dynamic load-control or throttling requirement is captured at requirements level.
This is a static clamping retention phase during drilling; a load-holding capability is required even though the actuator is horizontal and resistive.

Clamp release has no specified speed-control requirement and the user clarified the actuator is horizontal and resistive; retract motion is captured only as a required return/release action after drill retraction.

The stated drill feed speed is a numeric performance target only; no adjustability or load-independent feed control was specified, and the user clarified the drill feed axis is horizontal and purely resistive.
Retract speed is not specified and the user clarified the load is horizontal and resistive; retract motion is captured only as a required return action before clamp release.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit hydraulic power unit with system relief
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S feeds Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P, ClampDCV.P, and DrillDCV.P; ReliefValve.T, ClampDCV.T, DrillDCV.T, ForwardSequenceValve.T, and ReverseSequenceValve.T return to Tank.R. The pressure-compensated variable pump supports P-blocked valve neutrals and the relief valve provides system pressure limiting near the required maximum during sizing.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Clamp actuator with pilot-check load lock, vented-neutral hold, and reverse pressure-sequenced release
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ClampDCV extend supplies ClampCylinder.Cap through ClampLoadLock.A1-A2. In hold during drilling, ClampDCV float-center neutral vents both valve-side load-lock lines to tank so the dual pilot-operated check can reseat for low-leakage clamp holding. Clamp release/retract flow from ClampDCV.B is blocked until ReverseSequenceValve is piloted open by DrillDCV.B retract-supply pressure after drill retraction completion, then feeds ClampLoadLock.B1-B2 and ClampCylinder.Rod.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Forward pressure sequence with rod-side meter-out feed and free reverse retract
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: DrillDCV extend feeds ForwardSequenceValve.P. ForwardSequenceValve changes from closed to open after clamp extension has established clamp cap-side pressure at ClampLoadLock.A2 and ForwardSequenceValve.X. Once open, it supplies DrillCylinder.Cap. During drill-feed extension, DrillCylinder.Rod exhaust passes through DrillFeedFlowControl A-to-B to DrillDCV.B for the declared adjustable non-compensated meter-out control. During retract, DrillDCV.B supplies the rod side through the flow control's internal free reverse path and the drill cap side returns through ForwardSequenceValve's internal reverse check.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Hydraulic pressure sequencing without electrical sensing
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ForwardSequenceValve gates the drill cap work line and is selected closed during initial clamp extension, then open for clamp-hold/drilling after held clamp cap pressure is established at its X pilot. ReverseSequenceValve enforces drill-retract-before-unclamp using a pilot from DrillDCV.B, which is vented to tank during drill extension and pressurized only in the drill retract command path; it opens only after the drill reaches its retract end condition and retract-line pressure rises to the sequence setting. Both sequence-valve drains connect directly to Tank.R and their catalog reverse-check behavior preserves return paths.

design_decisions.decision: Change the forward sequence phase behavior so ForwardSequenceValve is closed during initial clamp extension and open in the clamp-hold/drilling and drill-feed phases after clamp pressure is established.
design_decisions.rationale: The pressure-sequence requirement must be demonstrated as a hydraulic state transition at clamp completion, not merely as a later command assertion. The X pilot is connected to ClampLoadLock.A2, the held clamp cap-side pressure downstream of the load lock, so the closed-to-open sequence-valve transition occurs between clamp_extend and clamp_hold_during_drilling.

design_decisions.decision: Move the reverse-sequence pilot from DrillCylinder.Rod to DrillDCV.B.
design_decisions.rationale: DrillCylinder.Rod is upstream of the meter-out flow control and can develop backpressure during drill feed extension. DrillDCV.B is on the return/tank side during drill extension and is pressurized during drill retract, so it avoids false clamp-release piloting from rod-side feed backpressure while still providing the retract-pressure signal used for pressure sequencing after the drill reaches its retracted end stop.

design_decisions.decision: Use a pressure-compensated variable pump with a float-center ClampDCV.
design_decisions.rationale: The clamp DCV neutral must vent A and B while blocking P so the load-lock valve-side lines can decay to tank during the hold/reseat phase. A pressure-compensated variable pump is compatible with blocked pressure ports and standby flow reduction.

design_decisions.decision: Install ClampLoadLock as a dual pilot-operated check at the clamp actuator ports.
design_decisions.rationale: The clamp must remain applied during drilling and DCV leakage alone is not acceptable. The dual pilot-operated check holds both clamp work ports during neutral/power-off conditions and is paired with ClampDCV float neutral so valve-side pilot pressure can decay.

design_decisions.decision: Place exactly one one-way flow control in the DrillCylinder.Rod exhaust path for drill-feed extension meter-out.
design_decisions.rationale: The immutable motion decision for drill_feed_extend is adjustable_throttled, meter_out, rod chamber, exhaust, non_compensated. DrillFeedFlowControl is wired DrillCylinder.Rod -> A -> B -> DrillDCV.B for extension exhaust, with internal free reverse flow from B to A for retract and no parallel bypass.

evidence_gaps.reason: The reverse interlock uses the supplied deterministic reverse-order pattern and catalog sequence-valve behavior, but the research synthesis did not cite a complete published schematic for this exact composed arrangement.
evidence_gaps.evidence_needed: Detailed hydraulic design review or an additional source showing the exact reverse pressure-sequence interlock arrangement.

assumptions: Cylinder bore, rod diameter, stroke, pump flow, relief setting, sequence-valve settings, and line-loss allowances are deferred to sizing.

ForwardSequenceValve is the selected externally piloted sequence valve; its X port is driven by ClampLoadLock.A2/clamp cap pressure downstream of the load lock, and its catalog reverse check preserves drill cap return from A to P.

The clamp_extend phase establishes clamp cap pressure at ClampLoadLock.A2; the following clamp_hold_during_drilling phase declares ForwardSequenceValve open to represent the hydraulic pressure-sequence transition at clamp completion.

ReverseSequenceValve is the selected externally piloted sequence valve; its X port is driven from DrillDCV.B rather than DrillCylinder.Rod so drill-feed meter-out backpressure upstream of DrillFeedFlowControl cannot falsely open the clamp-release gate.
ReverseSequenceValve setting is selected above normal drill retract moving pressure and below the pressure rise available when the drill cylinder reaches its retracted end stop.

The dual pilot-operated check uses the catalog conditional cross-pilot behavior: B1 pressure releases A2-to-A1 reverse flow, and A1 pressure releases B2-to-B1 reverse flow; no separate pilot ports are available in the selected catalog class.
During clamp_retract_release, DrillDCV remains in retract after the drill has reached its retract end stop to maintain the DrillDCV.B pilot pressure required to hold ReverseSequenceValve open.
open_issues: Sizing must reconcile clamp force, clamping permissive pressure near 3.3 bar, drill force, losses, and maximum pressure near 8 bar.

Sequence-valve settings and cracking tolerances must be selected during detailed design, especially the reverse sequence setting above drill retract moving pressure but below end-of-stroke pressure rise.
The external pilot from the clamp cap side to ForwardSequenceValve.X must be checked for allowable pilot leakage and any required isolation details during component selection.
The exact reverse-order drill-retract-before-unclamp schematic should receive detailed hydraulic design review because the supplied research did not include a direct complete schematic citation.
Phase 'clamp_hold_during_drilling' selects ForwardSequenceValve.open without pressure at X.
Phase 'drill_feed_extend' selects ForwardSequenceValve.open without pressure at X.

In phase 'clamp_hold_during_drilling', ForwardSequenceValve is declared open, but the directed phase behavior has no pressure path to its X pilot. Because the drill cap supply is gated by this valve, the topology does not prove the required hydraulic clamp-pressure permissive for drilling in the hold/drilling phase.

In phase 'drill_feed_extend', ForwardSequenceValve is declared open without pressure at X. Treating the directed phase invariant as failed, the forward sequence valve remains unavailable as a valid supply path, so DrillDCV.A cannot deliver the required sequenced supply to DrillCylinder.Cap for drill feed extension.

Because the forward sequence pilot is not pressure-proven in the active drilling phases, the topology does not satisfy the acceptance requirement that drill feed begin only after confirmed clamp contact/clamping pressure. The intended non-electrical pressure sequence is not functionally demonstrated by the directed phase paths.

research_coverage.summary: Most core hydraulic principles are supported with citations: open-circuit power/relief/return topology, clamp cylinder load-locking with pilot-operated checks, drill-feed meter-out flow control, and pressure-sequence-valve based clamp-before-drill actuation. However, two critical areas remain under-supported for a safe, unambiguous topology: the drill-feed directional-control neutral/porting pattern is not sufficiently cited, and the multi-actuator interlock/reverse-release sequence is only covered in the forward clamp-then-drill direction.

items.rationale: T1 provides cited guidance for reservoir-to-pump suction, pump pressure supply, actuator/valve return to reservoir, and relief valve from pressure line to tank/reservoir for overpressure protection. This is sufficient for the required open-circuit power and return path topology, though exact relief setting margin remains a design calculation rather than a topology need.

T2 supports a double-acting clamp cylinder controlled by a three-position directional valve, including work-port connections through pilot-operated checks and a cited neutral condition with A and B drained to tank so pilot-operated checks can close. This covers actuator/DCV pattern and safe neutral behavior for the clamp.

Clamp extend, hold, and retract/release components are partly supported: T2 covers clamp holding/release using pilot-operated checks and a DCV, and T4 covers automatic pressure transition after clamp pressure builds. The missing supported claim is the reverse/release sequence logic: the findings do not yet cite a topology that ensures the drill/feed actuator is retracted or otherwise safe before the clamp is released/retracted.

T2 provides cited guidance for pilot-operated check valves close to the cylinder ports, cross-piloted release, neutral A/B-to-tank behavior so checks close, and external drains where backpressure exists. This is sufficient for preventing unsafe clamp drift at the actuator.

T3 supports use of a double-acting cylinder and directional valve in principle, but its cited evidence is mainly about meter-out flow control. It does not sufficiently cite the directional-control valve porting for drill-feed extend/retract or the safe neutral center behavior for stopping/holding/unloading the drill-feed actuator circuit.

T3 gives cited support for meter-out speed control by throttling oil leaving the actuator, specifically rod-side exhaust during extension, and for a one-way flow-control/check arrangement that meters feed extension while allowing freer reverse/retract flow. T4 supports pressure-conditioned start of the drill/feed phase after clamping.

T4 strongly supports the forward hydraulic interlock: a normally closed pressure sequence valve prevents drill/feed flow until clamp pressure rises to the set value, with external drain and reverse check guidance. The missing supported claim is the complete forbidden-state/reverse interlock: evidence does not yet show how the circuit prevents clamp release while the drill/feed actuator is still extended or ensures drill retracts before unclamping.

T2 provides cited leak-resistant load-holding topology using pilot-operated check valves at the clamp cylinder, correct cross-pilot release, A/B-to-tank neutral to let checks seat, and external drain guidance. This supports keeping the clamp applied during drilling after force is developed.

T4 provides cited support for a pressure-operated, normally closed sequence valve that opens at an adjustable cracking pressure after clamp pressure builds, enabling drill/feed without electrical sensing. It also cites external drain requirements and clarifies that the valve is a sequencing/permissive element, not a downstream pressure regulator. This is sufficient for the pressure-conditioned clamp-to-drill transition around the specified pressure.

missing_or_weak_information: Missing cited drill-feed DCV porting and neutral-center selection: need support for how the directional valve connects P/A/B/T in extend, retract, and neutral for a double-acting drill-feed cylinder, including safe stop/unload behavior with the pump/relief topology.

Missing cited reverse/release interlock: need support for a hydraulic sequence that prevents unclamping while drill feed is extended, or ensures drill/feed retracts before clamp release, including any required sequence valves, check valves, pilot-operated checks, or valve-center logic.

design_issues.description: In phase 'clamp_hold_during_drilling', ForwardSequenceValve is declared open, but the directed phase behavior has no pressure path to its X pilot. Because the drill cap supply is gated by this valve, the topology does not prove the required hydraulic clamp-pressure permissive for drilling in the hold/drilling phase.

In phase 'drill_feed_extend', ForwardSequenceValve is declared open without pressure at X. Treating the directed phase invariant as failed, the forward sequence valve remains unavailable as a valid supply path, so DrillDCV.A cannot deliver the required sequenced supply to DrillCylinder.Cap for drill feed extension.

Because the forward sequence pilot is not pressure-proven in the active drilling phases, the topology does not satisfy the acceptance requirement that drill feed begin only after confirmed clamp contact/clamping pressure. The intended non-electrical pressure sequence is not functionally demonstrated by the directed phase paths.

The reverse drill-retract-before-clamp-release interlock is plausible using a second pressure sequence valve and the supplied deterministic pattern, but the research synthesis does not include a direct citation for the exact composed reverse-order schematic. This is nonblocking for generic topology, but should be reviewed in detailed hydraulic design.

design_review.summary: Invalid. The main functional failure is the forward pressure sequence: in the drilling/hold phases the directed phase model does not provide pressure at ForwardSequenceValve.X, yet the valve is selected open and is required to supply the drill cap line. As a result, the topology does not prove the required non-electrical clamp-pressure permissive or a valid drill-feed extend supply path. Other major requested elements—open-circuit power/relief, clamp load lock with vented neutral, drill rod-side meter-out valve, sequence-valve drains, and reverse release gating—are otherwise structurally represented, with only a nonblocking evidence gap for the exact reverse-order schematic.
